record.narrative: No claims or evidence exist yet, so the initial stage should generate falsifiable discovery comparisons rather than assess conclusions. I registered a breadth-first set of main-effect hypotheses across all outcomes, ordered so that the first 12 proposals cover distinct outcomes and likely enter analysis. Prevalent binary features (feature_008, feature_030, feature_047, feature_064, feature_023) are tested with direction +1, anticipating that the exposed=1 group may show weaker dependency (higher/less negative CRISPR dependency score), which is a plausible alternative to stronger dependency and therefore useful for broad exploration. Rarer binary features or the categorical level feature_054=level_002 are tested with direction -1, anticipating stronger dependency (more negative scores). Interaction hypotheses are registered for high-variance outcomes where heterogeneity among binary biomarker states is plausible: outcome_001 feature_034 effect modified by feature_002; outcome_006 feature_050 effect modified by feature_060; outcome_014 feature_054 effect modified by feature_045; and outcome_008 feature_045 effect modified by feature_034. For each, the anticipated interaction direction is negative, meaning the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is expected to be more negative in the biomarker-positive subgroup than in the complement. All initial statuses are unresolved because no data have been analyzed. Future assessments will require not only statistical exclusion of the null but also an effect size that is meaningful relative to the outcome scale and adequate cell counts. Any conclusions will be limited to this supplied dataset unless validated independently.

The ledger currently contains only unresolved registered hypotheses and no empirical evidence, so the most efficient next step is a broad discovery screen. I selected H1 through H12 because they span 12 distinct outcomes and test a mix of prevalent and rare binary predictors as well as one nominal categorical contrast. Running these main effects first provides the baseline association landscape needed to judge whether later interaction hypotheses (H17-H20) or refinements are worth analyzing. No assessments can be made yet because there is no direct evidence in the ledger.

I reassessed all new discovery evidence with the hypothesis-direction sign convention and the 10% relative-difference threshold. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates correspond to the hypothesized more negative dependency score; negative signed estimates indicate the opposite raw effect. H1-H5 and H9-H10 either had negligible point estimates, intervals that did not reach the clinically meaningful threshold, or intervals in the wrong direction, so I rejected and closed them. H6 is direction-consistent and its interval excludes zero, but its point estimate (~0.0195) is only about 8% of the outcome_007 mean and its interval crosses the 10% threshold, so I kept it unresolved and deferred while proposing a subgroup-specific refinement. H7 and H8 have wide intervals that cross the clinical threshold but no supportive point estimate, so I kept them unresolved and deferred. H11 is not supported as stated: its signed interval is entirely negative, implying a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast (weaker dependency) of about 0.038, roughly 15% of outcome_010. I rejected H11 and registered opposite-direction refinements for this promising but directionally reversed signal. H12 is the strongest active directionally consistent candidate: point estimate 0.048, about 11.6% of the outcome_001 mean, but the 95% interval includes zero and crosses the clinical threshold. I requested independent validation for H12. I also registered subgroup mean-difference refinements for H6 and H12 using feature_034, and for the reversed outcome_010/feature_006 signal. I deferred untested speculative interaction claims H17-H20 to reduce redundant use of analysis capacity. These conclusions remain associational; independent validation is intended to test H12 in an independent sample, not to establish causality or generalizability.

The newly delivered validation R13 for H12 (outcome_001, feature_001, direction -1) gives a signed estimate 0.0492, very close to the discovery estimate 0.0482 and above the approximate 10% clinical threshold for outcome_001 (~0.0415). However, the validation interval is extremely wide: lower -0.0765 and upper 0.1748, and it includes zero, so it does not independently confirm a statistically reliable or clinically meaningful difference. The validation sample also has a small exposed cell (n=99), which explains the low precision. Therefore, H12 should remain unresolved rather than accepted: the evidence is suggestive and replicates direction/magnitude in point estimate, but not sufficiently precise to claim a scientifically meaningful association in this dataset or to claim generalizability.

The initial broad discovery screen mostly produced negative or unsupported results: H1-H5, H9, and H10 are rejected/closed because estimates are small or intervals do not support clinically meaningful associations in the hypothesized direction. H11 as registered is rejected because its signed interval is entirely negative, implying the opposite raw effect. The opposite-direction claim H21 retains that evidence and is now the strongest remaining discovery candidate: outcome_010, feature_006 has signed estimate about 0.038, roughly 15% of the outcome mean, with interval excluding zero but still including sub-threshold values. I leave H21 unresolved and active because it deserves independent validation and subgroup/interaction follow-up rather than immediate acceptance.

For follow-up, I registered targeted refinements: outcome_010/feature_006 subgroup and interaction effects by feature_002 and feature_034, outcome_001/feature_001 subgroup effects by feature_034 (H24) and feature_002 (H28), and outcome_007/feature_042 subgroup effects by feature_034 (H23) and feature_002 (H29). These should determine whether promising overall signals are concentrated in measurable subgroups. The next analysis batch should also complete the untested broad main-effect screen H13-H16.

I registered new comparisons in two complementary layers. First, focused refinements of the most informative existing signals: outcome_010/feature_006 was rejected in the original direction but is a plausible opposite signal in H21, so I added mean-difference and interaction tests within feature_060 and feature_045 subgroups, expecting a positive raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast (weaker dependency, less negative score) if the signal is real and locally consistent. Outcome_001/feature_001 remains promising but imprecise, so I added feature_060 and feature_045 subgroup tests, anticipating a negative raw contrast (more negative dependency) if the effect is concentrated in those biomarker strata; interactions test whether the subgroup contrast differs from the complement rather than merely repeating the subgroup main effect. Outcome_007/feature_042 had a direction-consistent but subthreshold overall effect, so I registered feature_060 and feature_045 subgroup contrasts to test whether the association becomes clinically meaningful in measurable strata. I also registered an explicit reversal for outcome_014/feature_054 because H8's evidence, while imprecise, points weakly toward a positive raw contrast rather than the originally anticipated stronger dependency; this is a falsifiable alternative. Second, I added broad main-effect screens for high-variance or undertested outcomes using additional binary features: outcome_013/feature_014, outcome_008/feature_045, outcome_003/feature_021, outcome_006/feature_052, outcome_011/feature_022, and outcome_009/feature_046. These directions are mixed: rare-feature exposures often anticipate stronger dependency (negative raw contrast), while some prevalent-feature exposures anticipate weaker dependency (positive raw contrast), with uncertainty retained. I also changed H6 and H8 to active investigation because they now have concrete focused refinements. All proposed subgroup cells are expected to have adequate counts based on marginal prevalences, but empirical validity will be checked by the controller; if a cell is too small, no claim should be made from that comparison.

There are no assessments_due, so I made no scientific status changes in this analyze stage. I selected 12 claims to request discovery results from: H13-H16 complete the initial broad main-effect screen on four still-untested outcomes and common binary predictors; H40 adds one more moderately powered main-effect screen on the relatively high-variance outcome_008 using feature_045. The remaining seven claims are focused follow-ups on the strongest existing signals. For H21 (outcome_010/feature_006, positive raw contrast/weaker dependency), I test feature_034, feature_002, and feature_060 subgroup mean differences with H22, H25, and H30 to see whether the already-statistical effect is concentrated enough to be clinically meaningful in measured strata. For H12 (outcome_001/feature_001, negative raw contrast/stronger dependency), I test feature_034 and feature_002 subgroups with H24 and H28 because the overall point estimate is above threshold but imprecise and a concentrated subgroup effect would provide a more actionable association. For H6 (outcome_007/feature_042, negative raw contrast/stronger dependency), I test feature_034 and feature_002 subgroups with H23 and H29 because the overall effect is direction-consistent and statistically supported but below the approximate 10% clinical threshold. I prioritized mean-difference subgroup tests over interactions first so that each result can be judged directly against the outcome-level clinical threshold; interactions can be used later if subgroup estimates are promising.

The current appraise ledger shows no new valid discovery evidence attached to the claims that were pending follow-up analysis, so I cannot make new effect-size judgments for H13-H16, H22-H25, H29-H30, or H40. Those claims remain registered and active/unresolved unless and until valid intervals are delivered. I reassessed the strongest existing candidate, H21 (outcome_010, feature_006, direction +1), using R11. Its signed estimate is 0.0380, approximately 15.1% of the outcome_010 mean and above the approximate 10% clinical threshold of 0.0252. The 95% Welch interval excludes zero (0.0115 to 0.0646), but its lower bound is below the clinical threshold, so the supplied evidence supports a non-null but not unambiguously clinically meaningful association. Because H21 is a post hoc reversal of the original H11 hypothesis and the run has incurred multiple comparisons, I am not accepting it yet. I request independent validation for H21: if the validation interval is precise enough to exclude zero and has a lower bound at or above the 10% threshold, the claim becomes much stronger; if it is imprecise or subthreshold, H21 should remain unresolved or be downgraded. H12 remains unresolved after prior validation because discovery and validation point estimates are near threshold but intervals include zero. H6 remains active but lower priority because its overall effect is direction-consistent and statistically supported but below the clinical threshold. H8/H38 also remain unresolved because the reversal estimate is only marginally above the small outcome_014 clinical threshold and the interval is wide. All interpretations remain associational and dataset-specific; validation tests replication, not causality.

New validation R14 for H21 (outcome_010, feature_006, exposed 1 vs 0, direction +1) is not supportive of a clinically meaningful positive overall association. In hypothesis direction, the independent estimate is +0.0053, corresponding to only about 2.1% relative to the absolute outcome_010 mean, whereas the approximate 10% clinical threshold is about 0.0252. Its independent interval is wide: -0.0377 to +0.0484, so it includes both no effect and clinically meaningful positive effects, but it does not replicate the discovery point estimate. The discovery estimate R11 was +0.0380 (about 15.1% relative) with a 95% interval +0.0115 to +0.0646; although discovery excluded zero, its lower bound was below the clinical threshold and H21 was a post hoc reversal of H11. The validation result therefore substantially weakens confidence in an overall effect. I will not accept H21, but I also will not declare it definitively absent because the validation interval is imprecise and still crosses the threshold. I keep H21 unresolved but move it to deferred as an overall main effect. The most informative next analyses are the already registered conditional/interaction follow-ups for feature_006 (H22, H25, H26, H27, H30, H31, H32), which test whether any association is concentrated in measured strata, plus completion of the pending broad main-effect screens (H13-H16, H39-H44). Other current candidates remain unresolved rather than accepted: H12 has discovery and validation point estimates near the outcome_001 threshold but intervals that include zero; H6 is direction-consistent but below the outcome_007 threshold; H8/H38 is a weak reversal candidate with a wide interval. At this stage there are no claims that warrant acceptance as scientifically meaningful and reproducible associations in the supplied dataset or across independent samples. All interpretations remain associational; none imply causality.

No discovery evidence is due for assessment at this point, and the H21 validation failure has made the overall outcome_010/feature_006 candidate weak. I therefore propose the next high-information set without changing existing assessments. The new set follows three complementary strategies. First, I extend feature_042 across several dependency scores, beginning with outcome_014 and outcome_006, because the existing H6 evidence shows a direction-consistent effect of feature_042 on outcome_007 (raw contrast approximately negative) but only about 8% of the outcome_007 mean. The clinical thresholds are much smaller for outcome_014 and outcome_006—approximately 0.0093 and 0.0175 in absolute score units—so a similar raw contrast could be clinically meaningful there even though it is subthreshold for outcome_007. I also test feature_042 against outcome_013, outcome_001, and outcome_004 to determine whether the association is outcome-specific or broad. For outcome_001 I leave the direction uncertain because the threshold is large and the outcome variance is high. Second, I test common binary feature_034 and feature_002 for maximum statistical power. Feature_034 is present in nearly half the sample, making it the best way to detect a clinically meaningful main effect without the cell-size penalties of rare features. I test it primarily on outcome_011 and outcome_008, and also on outcome_014 and outcome_001; the outcome_014 claim uses the positive direction to reflect the weak but positive raw signal observed for the H8/H38 feature_054 reversal, while keeping expectation uncertain. Feature_002 is tested on outcome_013 as an additional common predictor. Third, I add two lower-specificity breadth tests: a nominal categorical comparison on outcome_014 using feature_019, and a common feature_060 test on outcome_012, which otherwise only has a closed negative screen. These claims are falsifiable main-effect associations, not causal claims. If a rare categorical level yields too few observations, the controller will mark the comparison invalid and it should not contribute to inference. Pending subgroup and interaction analyses remain useful, but after the H21 validation failure I prioritize well-powered main effects before requesting more validations.

No assessments are due, so I made no scientific status changes and selected the most informative untested comparisons for discovery. The prior validation of H21 weakened the overall outcome_010/feature_006 signal, so I deprioritized further feature_006 subgroup/interaction tests for now. I prioritize three high-value layers. First, H45-H47 extend the only current direction-consistent signal, feature_042, to outcomes with smaller absolute clinical thresholds and/or high variance: outcome_014 (threshold approximately 0.0093), outcome_006 (approximately 0.0175), and outcome_013 (approximately 0.0269). If feature_042 is a true biological predictor rather than an outcome_007-specific artifact, these comparisons should show either a broad association or a narrower, interpretable pattern. I leave outcome_004 and outcome_001 feature_042 tests for later because their clinical thresholds are similar to or larger than outcome_007's and they are less likely to add information immediately. Second, I test common predictor feature_034 on H50-H53 and feature_002 on H54 because common exposures give more balanced cells and narrower intervals than rare features. These cover outcome_011, outcome_008, outcome_014, outcome_001, and outcome_013 with well-powered main effects. Third, I complete pending high-information main-effect screens H13-H15 and add H56: feature_002 on outcome_008, feature_060 on outcome_003, feature_034 on outcome_006, and feature_060 on outcome_012. This set gives a focused but broad assessment of whether any measured predictor has a main effect large enough for the relative 10% clinical threshold and whether any candidate warrants validation.

The new feature_042 results are the most informative. H46 (outcome_006, feature_042, direction -1) gives a signed estimate of +0.0534, about 30.4% of the absolute outcome_006 mean and roughly three times the approximate 10% clinical threshold of 0.0175. The 95% Welch interval excludes zero (+0.0114 to +0.0954), so the supplied dataset supports a clinically large associational difference despite the lower bound being below the 10% threshold. Because feature_042 was already examined in H6 and H45, multiplicity is relevant; I therefore accept H46 as supported in this dataset but request independent validation before treating it as reproducible. H45 (outcome_014, feature_042) is suggestive, with estimate +0.0351 about 3.8 times the small outcome_014 threshold, but the interval crosses zero (-0.0012 to +0.0714), so it remains active but unresolved. H47 (outcome_013) is directionally inconsistent and weak; its interval also stays below the clinical threshold in the claimed direction, so it is rejected and closed. The feature_034 and feature_002 main effects H50-H54 and H54 show no clinically supported pattern. H50-H52 point estimates are far below their clinical thresholds, and the overall feature_034 evidence is now sufficiently uninformative to close these screens. H53, H54, H14, and H56 have intervals that do not reach the claimed clinical threshold and are rejected/closed. H13 (outcome_008/feature_002) and H15 (outcome_006/feature_034) have intervals that still allow clinically meaningful effects, but their point estimates and the multiplicity burden make them lower priority; I keep them unresolved but deferred. The validation request for H46 is intended to distinguish a genuine feature_042 effect from discovery-family false positive, not to establish causality.

The independent validation response for H46 changes the strength of the claim but does not overturn the discovery signal in the supplied dataset. Discovery R16 gives a signed overall contrast of +0.0534 for outcome_006, about 30.4% relative to the absolute mean and far above the approximate 10% clinical threshold of 0.0175, with a 95% Welch interval excluding zero (+0.0114 to +0.0954). Independent validation R27 gives +0.0182, only just above the threshold and with a wide independent interval (-0.0389 to +0.0751) that includes no effect. The validation is therefore not contradictory, but it is far less precise and does not replicate the discovery magnitude. I accept H46 only as a dataset-specific, clinically large association, not as a reproducible or generalizable effect. H12 reaches its response deadline: discovery and validation both point slightly above the outcome_001 threshold of about 0.0415, but both intervals include zero, so the claim remains unresolved and deferred rather than accepted. H2 validation confirms the absence of a clinically meaningful positive effect and keeps that screen closed. H6 is direction-consistent with feature_042 but remains below the outcome_007 clinical threshold, so I reject and close it as a clinically meaningful association. Overall, the strongest supported dataset-specific finding is that feature_042 is associated with lower outcome_006 scores. The feature_042 pattern is not yet coherent across outcomes: outcome_014 is borderline but unresolved, outcome_013 is inconsistent, outcome_007 is subthreshold, and outcome_001/outcome_004 remain untested. Most other common predictors are negative: feature_034 shows no clinically meaningful main effect, feature_002 and feature_060 are weak, and overall feature_006 lacks support. The most informative next analyses are the remaining feature_042 outcome-specific tests H45, H48, and H49, plus the new interaction proposal for whether the outcome_006 effect is concentrated by feature_034. These can clarify whether feature_042 is a broad predictor, an outcome-specific predictor, or a discovery-family false positive. All conclusions remain associational and dataset-specific.

No assessments are due in this explore stage, so I do not change any claim status. The current evidence makes feature_042 the only scientifically prioritized predictor: H46 is accepted as a dataset-specific clinically large association for outcome_006, while H45 is a very large but statistically borderline candidate for outcome_014. The main unresolved scientific question is whether feature_042 marks a broad dependency-score association, a narrow outcome-specific pattern, or a discovery-family false positive. I therefore register a coherent panel of feature_042 main-effect tests on the untested outcomes outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_011, outcome_012, and outcome_003. The negative direction is used because the signed H45/H46/H6 evidence implies lower raw scores in the feature_042-exposed group for the tested outcomes, and these are falsifiable predictions. If these outcomes show repeated negative differences above or near their 10% clinical thresholds, the feature_042 conclusion becomes much stronger. If most lower-variance outcomes are near zero, the accepted outcome_006 association is best interpreted as outcome-specific or possibly false-positive-prone. I also register two refinements of existing feature_042 claims rather than broad low-prior interactions: outcome_014 feature_042 modified by feature_034, parent H45, and outcome_006 feature_042 modified by feature_045, parent H46. These interactions ask whether the borderline outcome_014 signal or accepted outcome_006 signal is concentrated in an identifiable stratum. I include feature_045 as a common, reasonably powered modifier because it is less saturated than feature_034 and feature_002 in prior screens. Finally, I register a high-information broad screen for feature_045 on outcome_014 with uncertain direction because outcome_014 has the smallest absolute clinical threshold and feature_045 has about 510 exposed observations, giving a useful opportunity to detect a clinically meaningful main effect if one exists. I continue to avoid new feature_034, feature_002, feature_060, and feature_006 main-effect screens unless a subgroup effect is unusually strong. All proposed claims remain associational and dataset-specific.

No assessments are due, so I make no status changes. I select 12 comparisons that most directly resolve whether feature_042 is a broad dependency-score predictor or an outcome-specific discovery signal. Eight selected tests complete the feature_042 main-effect panel across previously untested outcomes (H48, H49, H58, H59, H60, H61, H62) and assess whether the outcome_006/feature_042 or outcome_014/feature_042 signals concentrate in identifiable subgroups (H64, H63). The remaining three are high-information common-predictor screens that add breadth and contextual information: feature_021 on outcome_003 (H41), feature_045 on outcome_008 (H40), and feature_045 on outcome_014 (H65). This set prioritizes the accepted candidate H46 and its borderline companion H45 while still permitting discovery of an independent clinically meaningful association.

I audited the new feature_042 panel and the follow-up predictor and interaction screens. The completed feature_042 panel does not support a broad clinically meaningful association across outcomes. H48 is statistically suggestive: signed estimate +0.0440 for outcome_001, just above the approximate 10% threshold of 0.0415, with a 95% interval excluding zero but also extending far below the clinical threshold. Given multiplicity across many feature_042 outcomes and the clinically imprecise lower bound, I keep it unresolved and active rather than accepted. H49, H58, H61, and H62 either have negligible point estimates or intervals that exclude a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. H59 and H61 include opposite-direction uncertainty but their point estimates are not clinically large, so I close those negative-direction claims. H60 has a wide interval allowing clinical effects, but the point estimate is small and the feature_042 outcome panel is otherwise null, so it is not a priority. The interactions are underpowered: H63 has a large positive point but a very wide interval crossing zero and the clinical threshold; it is useful only as a deferred hypothesis for the main feature_042/outcome_014 signal. H64 is too imprecise to support any interpretation and is closed. The non-feature_042 screens are mostly negative: H40 and H41 are not clinically supported, while H65 remains an active candidate because feature_045 shows a point effect above the small outcome_014 threshold, though statistically imprecise. For validation, H45 is the most scientifically consequential unresolved feature_042 claim: its point estimate is several times the outcome_014 clinical threshold and it is nearly statistically significant. Validating it directly tests whether the lead feature_042 signal extends beyond the already weakly validated H46.

New validation for H45 materially clarifies the feature_042 pattern but does not establish a reproducible effect. In the supplied dataset, discovery R15 gives a signed outcome_014 contrast of +0.0351 in the claimed lower-dependency direction, about 3.8 times the approximate 10% threshold of 0.0093, but its 95% interval is only marginally negative of zero on the opposite side (-0.0012 to +0.0714). Independent validation R41 remains directionally consistent at +0.0245, about 2.6 times that threshold, but its independent interval is wide and includes no effect (-0.0283 to +0.0773). I therefore keep H45 unresolved and defer further follow-up. It is scientifically suggestive but not a claim supported with adequate precision. Combined with the completed feature_042 outcome panel, this strengthens the conclusion that feature_042 is not a broad clinically meaningful dependency-score predictor in this dataset. H46 remains the one accepted dataset-specific finding: outcome_006 had a large discovery difference (+0.0534, roughly 3.0x the approximate threshold of 0.0175, interval excluding zero), while validation was weaker and imprecise (+0.0182, interval including zero). That is best described as a dataset-specific association, not a generalizable effect. H21 also reached its response deadline. The corrected positive-direction claim for outcome_010/feature_006 was significant in discovery (+0.0380, above the approximate threshold of 0.0252, interval +0.0115 to +0.0646), but the lower bound was below the 10% threshold and independent validation did not replicate the magnitude (+0.0053, interval including no effect). Because the direction was also post hoc relative to the originally rejected negative H11, I do not accept H21; it remains unresolved and deferred as a possible discovery-specific signal. H48 is the next highest-value unresolved feature_042 candidate: outcome_001 discovery is statistically significant and just above the approximate threshold (+0.0440 versus about 0.0415), but clinically imprecise. If further investigation proceeds, validation or a well-powered context test for H48 is more informative than additional feature_042 outcome screens. The two new proposals preserve focused follow-up: test whether the accepted H46 signal varies with common feature_002, and test the common feature_045 predictor in the lower-variance, accepted-signal outcome outcome_006 in the positive direction suggested by the feature_045 outcome_014 screen. All conclusions remain associational and dataset-specific.

No assessments are due, so I make no status changes and focus on the next scientific comparisons. The accepted dataset-specific lead remains H46, outcome_006/feature_042, with a large discovery difference but an imprecise independent validation. H48 outcome_001/feature_042 and H45 outcome_014/feature_042 remain the most clinically sized feature_042 follow-ups. The feature_042 panel so far does not support a broad negative-dependency effect, but outcome_008 has not been directly tested by feature_042 despite favorable cell sizes and a 10% threshold around 0.0282. I therefore register outcome_008/feature_042 in the negative raw direction, as expected if feature_042 marks stronger dependency; a null result would make feature_042 even more outcome-specific. I also register outcome_005/feature_042 as a lower-variance, adequately powered completion screen around the 0.025 threshold; this can either reveal a missed broad feature_042 effect or further constrain it. The feature_045 evidence is different: H65 for outcome_014 has a raw positive point estimate near its small clinical threshold, and the rejected H40 for outcome_008 had an estimated raw effect in the positive direction rather than the claimed negative direction. Because feature_045 has a large exposed group (about 510), I register positive main-effect tests on lower-variance outcomes with 10% thresholds near 0.025: outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_004. These are better powered than the noisy outcome_014 test and provide a coherent falsification panel. Similarly, feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 has a raw positive estimate near threshold on outcome_014 and a large exposed group (about 578). I register positive tests on outcome_012, outcome_009, and outcome_004. If feature_054 reflects a coherent weak-negative association, these outcomes should be more favorable for detecting it than outcome_014; if they are null, the outcome_014 signal is best treated as outcome-specific or noise. All new claims remain associational and dataset-specific. The most important priorities are to complete feature_042 evidence around H48, test whether feature_045 and feature_054 yield reproducible low-variance positive associations, and reserve validation slots for well-powered leads after these screens arrive.

No assessments are due, so I make no status changes and select 12 analyses that best advance the current evidence hierarchy. The first priority is to complete the feature_042 main-effect screen on the remaining medium/low-variance outcomes, outcome_008 and outcome_005, in the negative raw direction suggested by the accepted outcome_006 association. This gives the strongest remaining test of whether feature_042 marks a broad dependency-score association or remains narrow. The second priority is the feature_045 panel. Feature_045 already has a positive point estimate near the small clinical threshold for outcome_014 and a large exposed group, so testing outcome_006 plus lower-variance outcomes outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_004 provides a coherent positive-direction panel. If several clinically sized positive associations appear, feature_045 becomes a strong independent lead; if they are null, the outcome_014 signal is best treated as outcome-specific or noisy. The third priority is the analogous feature_054 panel: after the outcome_014 point estimate, test lower-variance outcome_012, outcome_009, and outcome_004 for a positive level_002 versus level_001 effect. These outcomes have smaller thresholds and better power than noisy outcome_014. Finally, I include three broad independent screens: feature_019 on the low-threshold outcome_014, feature_052 on the accepted-signal outcome outcome_006, and feature_046 on lower-variance outcome_009. These prevent the search from overfitting to feature_042 and preserve discovery breadth. After these results arrive, validation capacity should be reserved for any well-powered, clinically sized main effect that replicates the expected pattern, especially a feature_045 or feature_054 panel or H48 if the feature_042 pattern remains outcome-specific rather than broadly null.

I audited the new discovery evidence against the approximate 10%-of-absolute-outcome-mean clinical thresholds and the pre-registered claim directions. The main conclusion is that the new feature_045 and feature_054 screens do not reveal a broad clinically meaningful positive association. For feature_045, the outcome_006 positive claim H67 is rejected because the point estimate is in the opposite direction and far below the clinical threshold. The positive outcome_010, outcome_012, and outcome_004 tests H70, H71, and H72 are not clinically supported: H71 is opposite, while H70 and H72 have point estimates below threshold and confidence intervals that include both no effect and clinically sized uncertainty but do not provide enough evidence to continue as priority leads. For feature_054, the positive outcome_012, outcome_009, and outcome_004 tests H73, H74, and H75 are rejected as unsupported; the estimates are small, imprecise, or opposite. This leaves the earlier outcome_014-only signals as isolated low-threshold leads, but the lower-variance panel fails to corroborate them.

The new feature_042 screens sharpen the feature_042 interpretation. H69, outcome_005, is rejected as a small, statistically non-significant opposite-direction result. H68, outcome_008, is the only statistically significant new result, but its signed estimate is negative while the claim direction is negative: this means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive, not in the claimed direction. Interpreted on the raw scale, the effect is about +0.030 with a positive confidence interval around roughly 0.006 to 0.054. The point is only slightly above the outcome_008 threshold of about 0.028, and the lower bound is far below the clinical threshold. Given that this is a reverse-direction result from a broad outcome screen and not a pre-registered positive claim, I reject H68 as a negative-direction claim and close it; I do not treat the opposite signal as clinically established from these data alone.

H55 is the one new result worth retaining as a low-priority lead. Its point estimate for outcome_014 exceeds the very small threshold of about 0.0093, but the confidence interval is wide and includes zero and clinically meaningful values in both directions. I keep it unresolved and defer further work. The two broad screens H42 and H44 are rejected as unsupported.

For validation, I request independent validation of H48, outcome_001/feature_042. It remains the strongest unresolved pre-registered feature_042 claim: the signed estimate is about +0.044, just above the outcome_001 threshold of about 0.0415, and the interval excludes zero but is clinically imprecise. Validating H48 is more informative than validating the weaker or reverse-direction new screens. If validation replicates with a clinically meaningful magnitude, it would support a dataset-specific association; if not, it would further weaken the feature_042 pattern beyond the already accepted but weakly validated outcome_006 finding H46.

The new validation resolves the due claims and changes the feature_042 story materially. H46, outcome_006/feature_042, remains accepted in the supplied dataset as an associational finding. Discovery R16 is clinically meaningful in the claimed direction: signed estimate +0.0534, with 95% interval +0.0114 to +0.0954, above the approximate 10% threshold of about 0.0175 for outcome_006. Independent validation R27 is directionally consistent but weak: +0.0182, roughly at the clinical threshold, with a wide independent interval -0.0388 to +0.0751. Therefore H46 is supported as a dataset-specific association, not as a robust reproducible or generalizable effect, and it should not be interpreted causally. I keep it active because the most useful next question is whether the accepted outcome_006 signal is stable or concentrated within large common contexts.

H2, outcome_005/feature_030, remains rejected. Discovery R2 was small and in the opposite direction (-0.0141, interval -0.0402 to +0.0120), and validation R28 is near null/opposite (-0.0043, interval -0.0423 to +0.0337). This confirms no clinically meaningful association is supported.

H48, outcome_001/feature_042, is now rejected. Its discovery R29 was borderline: signed +0.0440 versus threshold about 0.0415, interval +0.0035 to +0.0844, but the lower bound was far below the clinical threshold.
